conventions.decision: AI full-text eligibility recommendation, distinct from final human/formal inclusion.
conventions.read_extent: Eligibility requires sufficient full-text evidence for every criterion, not independent verification of every proof, appendix or codebase. Inspected extent and version are specified per record.
conventions.features: Only feature_codes fields are verified in this checkpoint. Other legacy feature codes remain provisional. No means not demonstrated in the inspected evidence/version; Partial requires the stated limitation.
conventions.uq: Image UQ includes deterministic sets and posterior variability; it does not imply calibrated probabilities. Operator UQ requires uncertainty for operator parameters, not image variance caused by uncertain physics.
conventions.access: Full texts inspected online. No downloaded paper copies are added to the repository.
conventions.c1: All reviewed reports are primary research dated inside the existing search window; see version and canonical seed metadata.
conventions.c5: Every assessed record had an accessible English full text at source_url.
conventions.provenance: No reproducible database search or undocumented discovery date is inferred from this targeted batch.

records.title: NETT: Solving Inverse Problems with Deep Neural Networks
records.version: Inspected arXiv v3, 8 December 2019; journal lineage Inverse Problems 36, 065005 (2020), DOI 10.1088/1361-6420/ab6d57; final text not compared.
records.read_extent: §1.1; §§2.1–2.2 through Theorem 2.6 statement; §4 Algorithm 1; §§5.1–5.3. Proofs not audited.
records.technical: NETT combines a fixed forward operator with a trained regularizer. Stability/convergence statements require specified assumptions. Simulated photoacoustic experiments include phantoms outside the training class. They do not establish robustness to an incorrectly supplied operator.
records.applicability: Known-physics baseline; content transfer differs from operator mismatch.

records.title: Grounding Degradations in Natural Language for All-In-One Video Restoration
records.version: arXiv 2507.14851 v1 (2025); final WACV 2026 text not compared.
records.technical: Ronin distills training-time language embeddings into per-frame latent prompts. Synthetic compound video tests vary degradation intervals; held-out intervals differ from training. Physical operators and their uncertainty are not inferred. No inference-time language model is required.
records.applicability: Temporal-change comparator; interval transfer is narrower than an unseen acquisition family.

records.title: RestoreAgent: Autonomous Image Restoration Agent via Multimodal Large Language Models
records.read_extent: §§3.1–3.2.2; §§4.1–4.2 and §§4.4–4.6; selected Tables 1, 3–6. Supplement not fully audited.
records.technical: RestoreAgent plans restoration-tool sequences using a tuned multimodal model. Replanning and rollback are evaluated on compound corruption. records.title: DreamClear: High-Capacity Real-World Image Restoration with Privacy-Safe Dataset Curation
records.version: arXiv 2410.18666 v1 (2024); final NeurIPS 2024 text not compared.
records.technical: DreamClear combines generated training data, diffusion-transformer conditioning and token experts. Real-ESRGAN corruption and real benchmarks support compound restoration. Detection/segmentation are semantic-fidelity proxies. Training-image filtering does not establish test-time rejection of unreliable reconstruction.
records.applicability: Semantic fidelity and dataset curation are existing comparators.

records.title: SeeSR: Towards Semantics-Aware Real-World Image Super-Resolution
records.version: PDF header arXiv 2311.16518 v2, 4 June 2024; final CVPR 2024 text not compared.
records.technical: SeeSR distills degradation-resistant semantic prompts and initializes diffusion with low-resolution latents. Real benchmarks, false-detail illustrations and COCO tasks test fidelity. Tag thresholds select prompts, not reliable output regions; wrong tags under severe degradation remain a stated limitation.
records.applicability: Semantic preservation does not certify identity or fine-text truth.
